text:
elaine: Heads up — customer 'AcmePayments' hit decrypt failures and a big retry billing spike right after a scheduled KMS key rotation this morning. They claim key showed as rotated in console but their service started getting AccessDenied on Decrypt at ~08:12 UTC. CloudTrail in their account doesn't show RotateKey events for the key.

samir: ugh. do we have their key id/alias + rotation schedule?

elaine: alias: alias/acme-prod-transaction, key: 1234abcd-aaaa-4bbb-9ccc-98765example. Rotation turned on (console) at 08:00 by customer ops. They reported errors starting ~08:12 and retry flood from their worker pool.

marta: any error samples? encryption context mismatch vs AccessDenied?

elaine: sample from service logs: 
```
ERROR Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: Access denied
  status: 403
  operation: Decrypt
  keyId: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/1234abcd-aaaa-4bbb-9ccc-98765example
  encryptionContext: {"workspace_id":"ws-9"}
```
They show encryption context present. But when we asked for CloudTrail from their security team, RotateKey events are missing and their CloudTrail shows no kms.amazonaws.com SLR activity.

kevin: missing RotateKey in CloudTrail usually points at Service-Linked Role (SLR) or CloudTrail event selectors not capturing KMS events. If rotation was toggled from console, console should call EnableKeyRotation which triggers service to rotate annually — but the immediate scheduled rotation might require the SLR.

samir: check if svc role kms.amazonaws.com exists: 
```
aws iam get-role --role-name AWSServiceRoleForKMS
```
If it returns NoSuchEntity, rotation ops from console might be a no-op and manual rotation attempted? Also check CloudTrail event selector for ReadWriteType and includeManagementEvents.

elaine: customer ran that and got NoSuchEntity. CloudTrail shows management events = No for some trails. They have an org-level trail but management events disabled.

marta: that explains missing RotateKey event in CT. But why Decrypt started failing? Could be grant/token rotation race: when rotation flips key material, decrypt calls can still use previous key for ciphertexts encrypted with old material — KMS handles that normally. AccessDenied suggests either key policy or grant was changed during rotation, or encryption context was stripped by a proxy.

kevin: ask them for full KMS key policy history around rotation time. If rotation triggered a key policy reapply (some org tooling patches policies) it might drop principal or condition that enforces EncryptionContext.

elaine: they attached their audit snippet — at 08:01 a separate automation bot modified key policy to add org role but the JSON replace at 08:01 had an accidental Condition of StringEquals kms:EncryptionContext:ws that only matched ws-1..ws-8 (off by one). That would've denied ws-9.

samir: ok that seems likely: policy change + rotation coincident. But we need repro steps and mitigation so customer can recover quickly.

marta: repro steps to ask them to run in their account (minimal):
1) try decrypt with explicit encryption context omitted to reproduce AccessDenied. e.g.
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id 1234abcd-... --query Plaintext
```
2) try decrypt with correct encryption context shown earlier: 
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context workspace_id=ws-9 --output text --query Plaintext
```
If second works but first doesn't, that points at policy requiring context. If neither works, it's key policy denial.

kevin: for immediate mitigation if it's a policy condition error: roll back the key policy to previous version (if they have backups) or patch to remove erroneous Condition. If they can't, they can also create a temporary grant for the service principal performing Decrypt: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id 1234abcd... --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/acme-service --operations Decrypt
```
Grants bypass some policy constraints temporarily.

elaine: customer says they don't keep key policy backups (ouch). They can apply an emergency patch but want to know safe steps to avoid further rotation/ordering issues.

samir: also check whether any proxy or sidecar strips encryption context — network path logs show a haproxy in front of workers that stamps context in header; confirm worker actually sends it in KMS call. 

marta: logging commands to collect for AWS support:
- aws kms get-key-policy --key-id 1234abcd... --policy-name default
- aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/1234abcd... --start-time 2025-06-01T07:50:00Z --end-time 2025-06-01T09:30:00Z
- aws iam list-roles | grep KMS and aws iam get-role --role-name AWSServiceRoleForKMS
- list of grants: aws kms list-grants --key-id 1234abcd...
- CT config showing management events enabled/disabled for trails

kevin: if they have CloudTrail disabled for management events at resource level, need to enable or ask Support to surface rotation logs. For SLR absence they can create it: 
```
aws iam create-service-linked-role --aws-service-name kms.amazonaws.com
```
That should allow future managed actions to appear.

elaine: they did create SLR just now and re-enabled management events on org trail. AWS Support replied that EnableKeyRotation was never recorded so rotation did not actually run; what probably happened: customer automation tried to enable rotation AND simultaneously patched policy which introduced the bad condition — then some worker pool retried encrypt/decrypt with new expectations and started failing because of policy. Rotation not the root cause but timing made it look related.

marta: ok. final steps for remediation we recommended to customer:
- Immediately patch key policy to remove the erroneous Condition (or reapply known-good policy).
- If policy rollback impossible, create an explicit grant for their service role to allow Decrypt until policy fixed.
- Re-run failing decrypt with explicit encryption-context to test.
- If they used encryption context in SDK calls, confirm proxies don’t strip header.
- Enable management events on CloudTrail and ensure SLR exists so future key events are auditable.
- Run a non-destructive rotation test in staging: enable rotation, verify CloudTrail shows event, then decrypt sample ciphertext.

kevin: also ask them to check their retry/backoff config — the billing spike came from flood of retries. Suggest exponential backoff + circuit breaker.

elaine: AWS Support suggested we submit a formal request to re-run rotation if they desire (but warn they need to fix policy first). We advised them to fix policy and then we can help orchestrate a controlled rotation during low-traffic window.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-20250601-72 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-security and support.

samir: thanks — looping in oncall @kevin for follow-up with the customer to confirm policy patch.

kevin: I'm on it. I'll take contact channel and post remediation checklist to their support ticket. :thumbsup:

elaine: marking this thread resolved once customer confirms decrypts succeed after fix. keeping logs attached to the ticket.

aws-support-bot: Support case 987654321 opened with AWS; contact at aws-support@example.com.

marta: nice triage, clear action items.

kevin: update — they patched policy at 08:45, created a temporary grant, verified decrypts at 08:52, and we recommended a controlled rotation in 48h. closing loop with them now. :white_check_mark:
